llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed Chinese sales/fraud-prevention article generator that writes generated articles and a local HTML library, with notable but manageable concerns around broad triggers and off-platform paid-upgrade instructions.

dimensions.detail: The helper reads a user-supplied article file and writes an HTML library near that article directory, which is proportionate but should be pointed only at an intended content folder.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact contains one Markdown skill file and one local Python helper; there is no evidence of remote payload retrieval, dependency installation, or installer-time mutation.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Activation phrases are broad and the skill asks the agent to remember the article directory, so users should make sure they intended to run this workflow before files are created.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Persistence is limited to generated Markdown files, a local HTML library, and remembering the chosen directory; no services, scheduled tasks, privilege escalation, credential access, or system hooks were found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose, templates, compliance checks, article saving, and local library update all fit a daily content-production workflow.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you want a Chinese-language daily article workflow that saves Markdown files and updates a local HTML article library. Use a dedicated article folder, review generated content before publishing, and treat the WeChat paid-upgrade/payment instructions as external to platform protections.
llm.findings:
[SDI-4] expected: The free version is manual for duplicate and compliance checks but clearly discloses automatic local library insertion, so the apparent divergence is limited and not security-significant.
[SQP-1] expected: The trigger phrases are broad, but they relate directly to article generation; users should still confirm intent because the workflow creates local files.
[SQP-2] expected: Saving articles and updating the local full-text library are disclosed in the summary, description, and workflow steps, and are core to the skill's purpose.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The WeChat payment and screenshot workflow is not necessary for the free skill operation and creates privacy/trust concerns, but it is openly presented rather than hidden.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese output and a zh HTML template match the Chinese-language skill content and target workflow.
